Skytruth Analysis
(16SEP08) USCG PERSONNEL ON AN OVERFLIGHT TO ASSESS POST HURRICANE IKE WATERWAY CONDITIONS OBSERVED A TANK SHEENING IN THE NECHES RIVER WEST OF THE RAINBOW BRIDGE (RB). (17SEP08) USCG/TGLO LOCATED THE TANK FROM THE RB AND LAUNCHED A TGLO ASSET TO GATHER MORE INFORMATION. TANK IS HALFWAY UNDERWATER AND A VENT CAP (ABOVE THE WATERLINE) IS MISSING (SUSPECTED SOURCE OF SHEEN). TANK IS MARKED ON THE EXPOSED END WITH "17 DIESEL" AND IS STUCK WELL IN ABOUT 3' OF WATER 25-30 YARDS FROM THE NORTH BANK. AN ABSORBENT PAD WAS PLACED INSIDE THE OPENING TO REDUCE FURTHER DISCHARGE DUE TO TIDAL INFLUENCE.(19SEP08) USCG/TGLO RETURNED TO SITE. TANK IS STILL STUCK IN THE MUD AWAITING SALVAGE. NO SHEEN PRESENT AT THIS TIME.

properties.content:
Report Details

Medium Affected: AIR

SkyTruth Analysis
Lat/Long: 43.250795, -76.719468 (Approximated from street_address)
Report Description
CALLER STATED THAT THEY HAD A PRIVATE COMPANY CONDUCTED A $2500 AIR MONITORING TEST AT A PRIVATE RESIDENCE IN DEC2012 AFTER THEY HAD GOTTEN PROGRESSIVELY ILL THROUGHOUT THE TIME THAT THEY RESIDED THERE BETWEEN SEPT2000 - NOV2011. CALLER STATED THAT THEY NO LONGER LIVE AT THE RESIDENCE BUT STILL GO BACK TO THE LOCATION TO CHECK ON THE HOUSE AND ON 30MAR2012, TWO DOGS BECAME ILL AND WERE THROWING UP AND TWO FEMALES BECAME ILL WITH SYMPTOMS OF DIZZINESS AND THERE WAS A STRONG PETROCHEMICAL SMELL IN THE AIR. CALLER STATED THAT THEY LEFT THE AREA AND NOTIFIED THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT, BUT BY THE TIME THEY RESPONDED, THE WEATHER HAD CHANGED AND THE SMELL WAS NO LONGER PRESENT. CALLER STATED OVER THE COURSE OF THE 11 YEARS OF RESIDENCE, 5 INDIVIDUALS HAD NUMEROUS ILLNESSES AND SYMPTOMS AND WERE GOING TO A RANGE OF DIFFERENT DOCTORS AND URGENT CARE / EMERGENCY ROOMS. CALLER STATED THAT THE AIR MONITORING REPORT INDICATED THERE WERE LEVELS OF BENZENE - 5.3(NOTE CYCLOHEXATRIENE PPB1.6); METHYLENE CHLORIDE; TOLUENE - 36; ETHYL BENZENE; M, P, O, XYLENE; 1,3, 5 THIMETHYL BENZENE; 1,2,4 TRIMETHYLENE; P-ISOPROPYLTOLUENE; 1,2,3, TRIMETHYL BENZENE; NAPHTHALENE; FORMALDHYDE; ETHANOL; ETHYLACETATE; C4; ACETALDEHYDE; C4-C6 HYDROCARBON; ACETONE; ISOPROPANOL; 2- METHYLPENTANE; C5-C7 HYDROCARBON; C6, C6-C8 HYDROCARBON; 3 METHYLHEXANE; C7(HEPTANE 21 PPB); 1-BUTANOL - 1.8 PPB; METHYL CYCLOHEXANE - 1.4 PPB; ETHYLCYCLOPENTANE - 1.3 PPB; ETHYL ESTER OF BUTANOIC ACID - .5 PPB; N-BUTYLACETATE - 2.4 PPB; HEXANOL -1.0 PPB; A-D PINENE - .5 PPB; 2- BUTYLBUTOXY ETHANOL - 3.1 PPB; C-10 DECANE - .5 PPB; 6-METHYL-5-HEPTEN-2-ONE - .5 PPB; LIMONENE - 2.0 PPB; TOTAL V.O.C. - 640. CALLER STATED THE NY DEC RESPONDED THREE WEEKS PRIOR TO THIS REPORT AND STATED THERE WERE UNDERGROUND TANKS THAT WERE VERY CLOSE TO THE RESIDENCE THAT HAD LEAKED IN THE PAST BUT THE DETAILS OF THAT LEAK ARE UNKNOWN.

Report DescriptionCALLER REPORTS AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF CHLORINE, CHLORINE TABLETS, TILE CLEANER, ALGAE CONTROL CHEMICALS, POOL SCRUBBING CHEMICALS, AND FILTER CLEANERS HAVE BEEN LEFT OUT AND EXPOSED TO THE ELEMENTS IN A (03) WALLED SHED. WHEN IT RAINS THIS AREA FLOODS EASILY AND FLOWS INTO A BIG CONCRETE HOLE THAT CONTAINS AN ALLIGATOR. CALLER STATES THAT THE CHEMICALS CAN BE SEEN FLOATING ON TOP OF THE WATER AND POSSIBLY A NEARBY STREAM. THE SHED IS LOCATED BEHIND THE WAREHOUSE. THE MATERIALS ARE THERE BECAUSE THEY COULD NOT SELL THE PRODUCTS. THESE WERE ALL DISCARDED MATERIALS. THEY ARE LOOKING TO FIND A NEW WAREHOUSE AND HAVE STATED THEY WILL NOT CLEAN UP THE MATERIALS RELEASED.

WHILE WALKING ALONG THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER’S BANK (ALONG THE REVETMENT) ON JANUARY 5, 2011, SMALL SHEEN CIRCLES WERE OBSERVED ON THE WATER. UPON INSPECTION, IT WAS DETERMINED THE SOURCE MAY BE AN INTERMITTENT SEEP OF LIGHT NON AQUEOUS PHASE LIQUID (LNAPL) GLOBULES RESULTING FROM HISTORIC OPERATIONS AT THE FACILITY. THE SHEEN DISSIPATED QUICKLY AFTER FIRST APPEARING ON THE WATER. A SIMILAR INCIDENT OCCURRED ON NOVEMBER 10, 2010, AND WAS REPORTED TO THE NRC UNDER INCIDENT REPORT # 959615 AND LDEQ SPOC SYSTEM INCIDENT REPORT # GT01 8451. THIS AREA IS CURRENTLY BEING INVESTIGATED UNDER THE DIRECTION OF THE LDEQ (AI NO. 1708).
